text.p: Aboriginal groups who were the original signatories to an agreement to develop the A$1 billion Century zinc mine in the state of Queensland said on Friday they had withdrawn their agreement with mining giant RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd.

Three Waanyi tribe elders and two Mingginda tribe elders said in a statement that "inducements and undertakings" made to the remaining six aboriginal claimants to secure their signatures were the reasons for their decision to withdraw.

Talks on the mine's development collapsed in February following failure by the parties to obtain the required signatures of 12 aboriginal groups who were claiming land rights on areas surrounding the proposed mine in the northwest of the state.
The companies and aboriginal groups have now moved to the Federal native title tribunal for arbitration with the next meeting scheduled for April 21 in the northwest mining city of Mt Isa.
The aboriginals who withdrew their signatures said negotiations by other claimant groups were made without reference to the original signatories.

"We are concerned that those of us who dealt with the company and the (Queensland) state government in good faith are now being put in a detrimental position and those who have sought to delay the process are being rewarded," the aborigines said.
"We are extremely disappointed that we are now forced into a costly process of arbitration against our wishes," they said.

The aborigines said they had informed Australian Prime Minister John Howard, Queensland premier Rob Borbidge, RTZ-CRA, Century Zinc Ltd and the Aboriginal and Torres Straits Islands Commission (ATSIC) of their decision.
A spokesman for Century Zinc said there had been suggestions of a "side deal" being negotiated with the remaining aboriginal signatories for them to sign the original agreement.
"We have specifically rejected a claim for a consultancy fee to interests associated with the Willett claimant group," the spokesman told Reuters.
The original talks were focused on land rights under native title legislation and over a A$60 million compensation and jobs package which has now been withdrawn.

In January, base metals miner Pasminco Ltd said it would buy the Century Zinc and Dugald River zinc projects from RTZ-CRA for A$345 million, conditional on the Queensland government issuing mining leases which depend on Century Zinc and the aboriginal groups resolving the impasse over land rights.
